[LSIG.1.4.1] `onset_rate` is the number of rising edges per second within
the sliding window:

$\mathit{onset\_rate} = \dfrac{N_{+}(t, W)}{\min(W, \mathit{elapsed})}$

where `N₊(t, W)` is the count of rising edges whose instant lies in the
half-open window `(t−W, t]` and `elapsed = t − t_first` ([LSER.19.7]).

The runtime **must** count as a rising edge exactly the absorption of a `true`
while the slot holds `false`. The slot holds the value it last absorbed, through
any silence and whatever the window or capacity has discarded ([LSER.9.3.1]).
Before its first absorption it holds nothing, which is not `false`. An edge's
instant is that sample's.

tla.name: lsig_1_4_1__edges_are_transitions
tla.note: EDGES ARE TRANSITIONS, within the scope: the edges the engine counts are exactly the absorptions of a `true` whose predecessor among every absorbed sample is a `false`, so an edge is counted once per transition, a `true` after a `true` is none, and a first `true` is none, the slot holding nothing before its first absorption; the engine that holds `false` there is refused (`.teeth.first_true`). The predecessor is read off every absorbed sample and not the stored ones, as the clause has the slot hold its value through whatever the window discarded. That an edge's instant is its sample's is `lsig_2_2_4__edges_share_the_sample_window`.
